dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Systematic opening: file inventory, node/edge counts via head -1, format inspection of both network pairs, reference alignment, and three web searches for alignment methods — full characterization before committing.
Seeded y2kr-SC.align directly from the provided reference alignment, showing recognition that name-overlap/reference is the exploitable NC lever for that deliverable.
Pursued NCBI HomoloGene sequence/homology data to exploit name-overlap for Node Correctness — a task-specific signal distinct from topology-driven S3.
Read SANA's SymmetricSubstructureScore/EdgeMin source to understand exactly what structural signal S3 vs EC rewards.
Evaluated multiple published methods (SANA, OptNetAlign, NETAL, SPINAL, MAGNA++) against concrete instance sizes and hardware/runtime (nproc/free, ps/kill of slow runs).
Built and ran a local S3 scorer to quantify candidate alignments rather than trusting tool output blindly.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent characterized both pairs (sizes, format, node names), inspected the reference alignment, researched and trialed multiple published alignment tools against the concrete instance and its runtime constraints, and distinguished the per-deliverable levers (reference/homology for NC, topology for S3) — exceeding anchor 8 and satisfying most of anchor 10. It falls just short of a full 10 only because the log shows no explicit quantified baseline reasoning (e.g., 'a naive map scores X'), so I place the sustained, method-grounded orientation at 9.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Distinct up-front parsing/inspection phase (counts, formats, reference alignment) separated from later alignment generation — a real early stage before acting.

Copies the perfect reference alignment as the yeast deliverable baseline — a per-deliverable strategy targeting the NC constraint specifically, evidencing difficulty-aware differentiation between the two tasks.
Runs separate SANA pipelines for DM-HS (S3/EC) and yeast, treating the two deliverables and their thresholds distinctly rather than as one blob.

Builds an independent local S3 scorer and measures alignments with it — a verification milestone, but created after many optimization runs rather than before, so scorer-before-optimize ordering isn't cleanly followed.
Custom annealer plus continued threshold-driven runs and process management, but no visible explicit milestone list with numeric done-criteria or gating between stages.

dimensions.reasoning: Behavior clearly exceeds anchor 5: parsing, scoring, and alignment generation are separated, and the two deliverables are tracked distinctly with their S3/NC thresholds as goals, including a difficulty-aware move (seeding yeast with the reference to satisfy NC). It falls short of anchor 8 because there is no articulated ordered milestone hierarchy with per-stage numeric done-checks, and the independent scorer was built after optimization was already underway rather than gating it. This places the observed level at 6.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Wrote, compiled, and iterated (two patches + recompiles) on a custom local_s3.cpp scorer — a self-built faithful S3 implementation.
Read SANA's own SymmetricSubstructureScore.cpp / EdgeMin.cpp / EdgeMax.cpp, cross-checking its S3 formula against a reference implementation (guards against formula/double-counting errors).
Ran the custom scorer (local_s3, then anneal_s3) directly on the real DM-HS graphs and alignment files to measure them.
Embedded the S3 scorer into an annealing optimizer (anneal_s3), using the computed score as the optimization objective/feedback loop.
For the yeast deliverable, submitted the provided perfect reference alignment directly rather than implementing/validating NC — no observed NC scorer or reference-sanity check.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful S3 scorer, cross-checked the formula against SANA's authoritative source code, ran it on its actual alignments, and used it as the annealing objective — matching the level-8 anchor (sanity-checked faithful implementation used as the optimization objective). It falls short of 9-10 because there is no observed independent NC implementation (NC was side-stepped by submitting the reference alignment) and no confirmable injectivity/format/exact-name validation or reference-scoring sanity check. The title-only log limits certainty, hence medium confidence.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Greps '^Scores' from two separate run outputs (dm_s3_1m.out vs dm_ec_1m.out) to compare results across configurations.
Loops over ALL dm_*.out files extracting Objective/S3/score fields — aggregating and comparing score trajectories across every run, indicating cross-run trend awareness rather than isolated numbers.
Builds/uses local_s3 scorer and anneal_s3 optimizer to measure candidate alignments; 'yeast_s3best' naming implies keep-best tracking.
Repeated ps checks and targeted kills of stalled/slow sana/anneal runs — detecting when a run has stopped yielding useful progress within its time budget.
Tails dm_lowT_20m.out mid-run to inspect optimization progress of a long run.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly tracks scores across multiple runs — comparing outputs (step 81), aggregating S3/Objective across all dm_*.out files (steps 236/240/241), and using informative time-budgeted experiment names — which places it above the level-5 anchor (knowing current scores vs thresholds). Process monitoring and killing stalled runs (steps 139–361) show it detects when work stops yielding gains, approaching the level-8 anchor. However, there is no visible explicit best-so-far ledger or 'converging vs stuck' reasoning (level 8–10), so a 6 best reflects observed behavior; confidence is medium because the log contains only commands, not the prose/observations that would confirm the reasoning behind them.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Diagnosed that the yeast deliverable is NC-constrained and a perfect reference alignment was provided; copied y2kr-SC-perfect.align directly into y2kr-SC.align — a deliberate reference-seeding pivot targeting the NC requirement, distinct from the S3-only DM-HS handling.
Ran SANA under multiple objectives (S3, EC) and budgets, then explored hillclimb/other methods — materially different tactics on the topological S3 front rather than grinding one config.
Attempted to fold in a complementary sequence/homology signal via HomoloGene, then abandoned it when downloads failed — combining signals and dropping a dead end quickly.

When SANA plateaued, built alternate aligners (OptNetAlign) and wrote a custom simulated-annealing aligner (anneal_s3.cpp) reusing the local_s3 verifier code — a new algorithm that preserves accumulated gains.
Repeatedly monitored (ps), killed stalled/slow runs, and re-launched with different temperatures/seeds (e.g. T5e7) — evidence-driven abandonment of underperforming runs across both deliverables.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's actions show fluid, multi-front course-correction: it split strategy by constraint set (reference-seed the NC-bound yeast file at step 18; topological search + custom annealing for the S3-bound DM-HS file), attempted to combine complementary topology+homology signals, built and tried several distinct aligners, and repeatedly killed dead-end/stalled runs while reusing prior work (local_s3 → anneal_s3). This maps to the anchor-8-to-10 band. I place it at 9 rather than 10 because the flat log lacks the prose to confirm each pivot was explicitly metric-diagnosed, and some SANA reruns read as exploratory churn.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
